Stream2Vec pipeline benchmark document

This document is used to measure end-to-end processing time for Stream2Vec.
The unique token for retrieval tests is AURORA-NEXUS-7741.

Stream2Vec ingests documents through a FastAPI API, stores the raw bytes in MinIO,
publishes a Kafka event, then Apache Spark extracts text, cleans it, splits it into
overlapping chunks, generates sentence-transformer embeddings, and upserts vectors
into Qdrant. PostgreSQL keeps document metadata and processing status.

Aurora Nexus is a fictional industrial monitoring platform. Its command center is
located in Lyon, France. The on-call rotation uses the pager code AURORA-NEXUS-7741.
The primary sensor bus is named Helix Bus. Helix Bus samples temperature, vibration,
and humidity every five seconds. Alerts fire when vibration exceeds 12.4 millimetres
per second for more than thirty seconds.

The recommended maintenance window is Tuesday 02:00 to 04:00 UTC. Spare parts for
the Helix Bus gateway are stored in warehouse bay K-19. The gateway firmware version
used in this document is 4.8.2-stable. Network traffic between gateways and the
command center uses MQTT over TLS on port 8883.

Retrieval-augmented generation should be able to answer questions such as:
- What is the pager code for Aurora Nexus?
- Where is the command center located?
- What firmware version does the Helix Bus gateway run?
- When is the recommended maintenance window?

Additional filler paragraphs follow so the chunker produces several chunks.

Quality control procedure: operators inspect Helix Bus gateways after every firmware
update. They verify that MQTT certificates are valid for at least sixty days, that
disk usage on the gateway stays below seventy percent, and that the watchdog process
named nexusd is running. If nexusd is not running, operators restart it with the
service manager and file an incident tagged AURORA-NEXUS-7741.

Capacity planning notes: a single Spark worker with two cores and two gigabytes of
memory can embed short documents with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 in a few seconds after the
model is warm. Cold start is dominated by downloading the model weights and by the
Structured Streaming trigger interval. Kafka micro-batch delay is therefore part of
the observed wall-clock latency.

Security notes: MinIO credentials must not be committed. Qdrant authentication is
disabled in local development and must be enabled in production. Kafka is deployed
in KRaft mode without ZooKeeper. PostgreSQL stores only metadata, never raw file
bytes. Raw files remain in the documents bucket.

Operations runbook: if a document stays in pending status, check that spark-job is
running, that the Kafka topic documents.raw exists, and that the Spark checkpoint
directory is writable. If status is failed, read error_message on the document row.
If status is processing for more than ten minutes, inspect Spark executor logs for
MinIO download errors or embedding failures.

Closing paragraph: AURORA-NEXUS-7741 is the unique retrieval token. Lyon is the
command-center city. Helix Bus firmware is 4.8.2-stable. Maintenance is Tuesday
02:00 to 04:00 UTC. Warehouse bay K-19 holds spare gateways.
